new_findings.finding: Every Overloaded refusal asks for the same constant 1 s (OVERLOAD_RETRY_AFTER), and the client follows a server-directed delay exactly (min max_backoff) with no jitter; only its own computed backoff is jittered.
new_findings.scenario: 1,000 supervisors with RetryPolicy::default() hit one saturated worker: all refused sends return at t+1 s, t+2 s, t+3 s in synchronized waves, re-saturating the worker each time instead of spreading out.

new_findings.finding: Delegation resume (ADR 0030, built) reopens immediately on the first attempt and then backs off deterministically (0, 200, 400, 800 ms ... no jitter, pinned exactly by the unit test at resume.rs:302-319). Each reopen is a SubscribeToTask, which RetryTransport also retries (idempotent method) when the client has a retry policy, and each failed reopen adds a GetTask: up to 5 x 4 subscribe attempts per loss.
new_findings.scenario: An L4 balancer or proxy rollout resets 10k delegation streams at once: 10k SubscribeToTask (each a task read plus a log replay on the server) arrive at the same instant, then again in lockstep waves.

new_findings.finding: A lease renewal is a full GetTask: the server reads the whole task row, renews, and, with a content signer (required by Profile::Production), signs the status message and every artifact before returning them all; the client then runs content verification over the answer. history_length=0 (the report's quick fix) trims history only; artifacts are always returned and signed.
new_findings.scenario: A production-profile worker holding children with large artifacts (up to 1000 artifacts x 10k parts) pays an Ed25519 signature and a full serialization per artifact per renewal, every ttl/3, per child.

new_findings.finding: A halt-store row whose scope key is unknown makes from_row fail, which fails the whole load. A running replica's poller then keeps the halts it last read (and stops seeing new halts and resumes of every scope); a replica that starts while such a row exists can never sync and refuses every send.
new_findings.scenario: ADR 0034 adds HaltScope::Root (or any new scope). During a rolling upgrade, or with one org-wide halt table shared by services on different SDK versions (which ADR 0034 proposes), one root halt freezes halts on every older replica and takes restarted older replicas out of service.

new_findings.finding: start_journaled wraps only Delegation::start, so a journaled delegation cannot also be leased or budgeted through the API (the private Renewal cannot be started afterwards); attaching a lease to the message by hand gives a child that nobody renews. reattach also leaves renewal None. Composing by hand (journal.begin, start_leased, with_journal) is possible but undocumented.
new_findings.scenario: A supervisor uses the journal (to survive restarts) and leases (to survive crashes). After a restart it reattaches its children, but nothing renews their leases, so the server cancels each leased child within its TTL: the restart the journal exists for kills the children it recorded.

new_findings.finding: TaskStore::save_appending_history's doc says 'the SQL stores splice the tail into the stored document'; neither PostgresTaskStore nor SqliteTaskStore overrides it (only in-memory, encrypted, traced and audit do), so SQL sends take the O(history)-twice default.
new_findings.scenario: An integrator reading the trait docs assumes SQL appends are O(1) and sizes a long-lived channel task accordingly; swarm-scale Finding 7 shows the ageing.

new_findings.finding: Until the halt store has been read once, every send is refused as ServerError::Halted('the halt store could not be read'), which goes out as -32603 with no RetryInfo on JSON-RPC (non-retryable for the client) and 503 on REST, while /ready keeps answering 200. Each refused send retries the load under the sync lock (with the store's own retry), so sends also queue behind it.
new_findings.scenario: Production profile (halt store required) with the halt store on a database that is unreachable when a replica starts: the replica stays in the Service, every caller gets a final 'halted' error for an outage, and sends pile up on the lock.
